name: nix-develop
description: Select a devShell from your flake.nix and reopen the workspace inside it, with the editor running in nix develop.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Evaluating a flake executes arbitrary Nix code and shell hooks from the workspace.

nixDevelop.flakeDirectory.markdownDescription: Directory containing `flake.nix`, relative to the workspace folder.

nixDevelop.promptWhenUnset.description: Prompt to pick a devShell when a flake.nix is present but no devShell has been selected yet.

nixDevelop.extraArgs.description: Additional arguments passed to nix develop.

nixDevelop.buildTimeoutSeconds.description: Abort the devShell build after this many seconds.

enumDescriptions: Keep a Nix profile per devShell under .vscode/nix-develop/, and leave it there. The built shell survives `nix store gc`, so reopening the folder -- offline, or after a garbage collection -- costs nothing. The directory is gitignored for you; delete it to release the store paths.

Pass no --profile. Nothing roots the devShell: `nix store gc` may collect it between building the shell and starting the server, and will collect it once the server exits. Nothing is written into the project.
nixDevelop.profile.markdownDescription:
How the built devShell is kept alive against `nix store gc`.

`--profile` is the only thing that makes a devShell a GC root. `persistent` writes one per devShell under `.vscode/nix-develop/<devShell>/` -- next to the project, with a `.gitignore` covering the whole directory -- and never removes it, so the toolchain a window needs is still there after a garbage collection or on a flight. `none` writes nothing into the project and accepts that the shell may be collected; on Linux, Nix's GC still spares store paths a *running* process references, so this mostly costs you rebuilds rather than a broken window.

enumDescriptions: Stream the build into a terminal and show it as soon as the build starts. The terminal stays after the window opens.
Stream the build into a terminal, but bring it into view only if opening the devShell fails. On success the terminal is closed again.
Collect no build output. Nix is run with its default log format and only the progress notification is updated.
nixDevelop.showBuildOutput.markdownDescription:
Whether to show what `nix develop` is doing while a devShell window opens.

The devShell is built before the editor's server starts, so downloads, compiles and the evaluation error that says which attribute is missing all happen there. The output goes to a terminal named after the devShell, with Nix asked for `--log-format bar-with-logs` so the full build logs arrive rather than the handful of lines Nix prints by default.

nixDevelop.remote.serverDownloadUrl.markdownDescription: Where to fetch the editor's server. Leave empty to detect it: VSCodium and other rebuilds declare their own `serverDownloadUrlTemplate` in `product.json`, and Microsoft builds fall back to `update.code.visualstudio.com`. Set this only to override that. The placeholders `${commit}`, `${quality}`, `${version}`, `${os}`, `${arch}` and `${platform}` (`${os}-${arch}`) are substituted.

nixDevelop.remote.connectTimeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the devShell server to report a listening port.

nixDevelop.remote.patchServerLd.markdownDescription: Point the devShell server's bundled `node` at a glibc from nixpkgs, using `patchelf`. The server ships a `node` linked through `/lib64/ld-linux-*`, which NixOS does not have. Turn this off on a host that resolves that path on its own -- `programs.nix-ld` enabled, or not NixOS at all -- to leave the binary alone and build nothing from nixpkgs.
